subject.title: Google Chat: agent-to-agent (bot↔bot) conversation doesn't work — a Chat app doesn't receive messages from another Chat app (same setup works on Discord)

question: Should OpenClaw handle this Google Chat app-to-app gap as docs-only, or should maintainers sponsor an explicit channel-independent A2A bridge?
rationale: The narrow docs clarification is straightforward, but an automatic bridge would add product semantics across agent routing, loop prevention, and message provenance that source inspection alone cannot choose.

options.title: Document the limitation first
options.body: Add a Google Chat and multi-agent docs caveat that peer Chat-app messages may not arrive, while leaving bridge design for a later explicit proposal.

options.title: Sponsor an opt-in bridge design
options.body: Define how logical agent mentions map to sessions, which policy gates apply, and what live proof is required before implementation.

options.title: No product change
options.body: Keep relying on explicit `sessions_send` and channel-native delivery, accepting that Google Chat app-to-app conversation is unsupported.

recommendation.title: Document the limitation first
recommendation.body: Add a Google Chat and multi-agent docs caveat that peer Chat-app messages may not arrive, while leaving bridge design for a later explicit proposal.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses bot-loop protection and multi-agent routing surfaces where `steipete` has the clearest feature-history signal.
